observations: A large frontal head shape dominates the center, with two circular eye forms filled with dense hatched lines — one square-ish in yellow and black, one round with a red X over blue and orange.
Jagged crown-like points rise along the top edge in black and yellow, flanked by orange and green drips running down from the upper border.

The lower third shows a wide open mouth form in dark red with white horizontal lines suggesting teeth, set against a gray background crossed by yellow scribble lines and a small artist mark in the lower right.
reading: The face pushes forward on a gray field, its two mismatched eyes — one gridded, one crossed out — giving the image an off-balance stare that reads as confrontational or unsettled. Drips from the top border and the open-toothed mouth below pull the eye up and down at once. Scrawled lines layered over flat color blocks create a surface that feels both raw and packed.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, the title neighbors are nnxyz nnotb #235 and nnxyz nnotb #237; title order and recorded creation order align here. The collector links nnxyz to scrimshaw through shared pattern density and emotional range.

connections.reason: nnxyz nnotb #237 shares the single centered head format and a crossed-eye motif on a dark ground, but replaces the gray field with a warm yellow-ochre surround, making the color contrast between the two works direct and visible.
nnxyz nnotb #235 uses the same circular eye-within-eye construction and open-mouth form, but spreads two heads across a busier, warmer background rather than isolating one face on gray.

lookingQuestion: The two eye forms are built differently — one gridded and square, one circular with an X — what does that asymmetry do to how you read the face as a whole?
